archetypes.name: cross-ref-integrity
archetypes.rationale: Plan cites specific field-line predicates, counting-rule names, flag shapes, and header triplet field names across oos-non-security-block-count.awk, oos-disposition-gate.md, oos-disposition-checkpoint.sh, and test-references-headers.sh; if any of these differ from the actual repo files the new reference will silently carry wrong contracts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every external file, awk script, and helper contract the plan cites actually exists in the repository with the described interface. Check that the security-routing predicate in plan step 1 — dedicated `- **focus-area**:` field-line, case-folded, `security[-word]` prefix match — matches the actual pattern in `skills/implement/scripts/oos-non-security-block-count.awk` and the Counting-rules section of `skills/implement/scripts/oos-disposition-gate.md`. Confirm that `oos-disposition-checkpoint.sh` accepts a `--filed-urls-file` flag and that its URL-token grep shape is compatible with the sentinel format the plan pins (table header `| OOS title | Issue | URL |`, `- **Filed**: <N>` tally, `issues/<n>` token). Verify that `scripts/test-references-headers.sh` enforces exactly the Consumer/Contract/When-to-load triplet field names — not different header names — so the new file's triplet will actually pass the check. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: never-rule-reconciliation
archetypes.rationale: Plan proposes a targeted NEVER #5 narrowing (sentinel-recovery writes only oos-issues, not run-statistics) while asserting NEVER #14 already owns post-checkpoint stats; contradictions between the current NEVER text and the proposed change could leave the sentinel-recovery run-statistics prohibition ambiguous or create new gaps.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the verbatim text of NEVER #5 and NEVER #14 in `skills/implement/SKILL.md`. Determine whether the plan's proposed NEVER #5 narrowing — sentinel-recovery branch writes only the `oos-issues` larch-log append, not `run-statistics` — is consistent with both the current NEVER #5 body and NEVER #14's post-checkpoint stats ownership claim. Identify any wording in the current NEVER #5 that explicitly instructs a sentinel-recovery `run-statistics` write, and confirm the plan's approach removes exactly that instruction without silently invalidating unrelated NEVER #5 guidance. Verify that after the plan's changes no NEVER rule text would instruct writing `run-statistics` before `oos-disposition-checkpoint.sh` passes on any code path, including both the sentinel-recovery branch and the normal filed path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
